what: Feature pre-processing and model configuration using fl_rfsetup() and fl_cvsetup()
title: Forced labor risk workflow on a sample dataset
text: Following tidymodels framework, function fl_rfsetup() calls recipes package functions preprocess training dataset, specifying roles transformations model features. Importantly, distinguishes features used predictors, one response variable one used control variable avoid data leakage. Vessel MMSI (Maritime Mobile Service Identity) –can appear several related cases–thus used control variable data leakage (vessel-year cases vessel assigned either training holdout dataset). corresponds column ssvid. Feature transformations included removing near-zero variance variables recipes::step_nzv() removing highly correlated variables (correlation value can setup parameter corr_threshold). fl_rfsetup() also calls parsnip package specify hyperparameter values RFs, number trees, number features sampled split, minimum node size regularization factor. chosen model engine one package [ranger]. function returns list two elements corresponding setup : $rf_recipe, output recipes $rf_spec RF specification parsnip
code: features_model_characteristics <- c("gear",                                     "engine_power_kw",                                     "tonnage_gt",                                     "length_m") features_model_movement <- c("position_messages",                              "hours",                              "fishing_hours",                              "average_daily_fishing_hours",                              "fishing_hours_foreign_eez",                              "fishing_hours_high_seas",                              "max_distance_from_shore_km",                              "max_distance_from_port_km",                              "number_encounters",                              "number_forced_labor_encounters",                              "average_encounter_duration_hours",                              "gaps_12_hours",                              "average_off_distance_from_port_km",                              "average_off_distance_from_shore_km",                              "average_gap_days",                              "average_gap_km",                              "number_foreign_port_visits",                              "number_loitering_events",                              "average_loitering_duration_hours",                              "average_voyage_duration_hours",                              "number_voyages")  rf_setup <- fl_rfsetup(training_data = training_df,                        y = "known_offender",                        x = c(features_model_characteristics,                              features_model_movement),                        id = "indID",                        dont_use = c("known_non_offender"),                        control = "ssvid",                        corr_threshold = 0.75,                        rf_trees = 500,                        rf_mtry = 5,                        rf_min_n = 10,                        rf_reg_factor = 1)

what: Function fl_classification(): density-based algorithm for classification
title: Forced labor risk workflow on a sample dataset
text: threshold fl_classification() aggregates RF scores row, estimates α\alpha (upper bound positives unlabeled set) estimates threshold t proportion predicted positives ≈ α\alpha. See (Ivanov 2020) details DEDPUL algorithm. Within fl_classification() apply calibrated threshold t vessel’s mean RF score (pred_mean): pred_mean > t, pred_class = 1, else 0. produces binary prediction (positive negative, stored column pred_class). confidence value indicates consistently vessel’s score falls side t across seeds × bags. Values near 1 indicate stable classification vessel-year (.e. higher confidence classification). case sample dataset, 10072 vessel-years classified negative 55 classified positive forced labor risk.
code: tictoc::tic() classif_res <- fl_classification(data = prob_all,                                  steps = 1000,                                  plotting = FALSE,                                  filepath = NULL,                                  threshold = seq(0, .99, by = 0.01),                                  eps = 0.1,                                  confidence_levels = TRUE                                  ) #> [1] "alpha:  0.0530530530530531" tictoc::toc() #> 11.862 sec elapsed class_pos <- sum(classif_res$pred_conf$pred_class == 1) class_neg <- sum(classif_res$pred_conf$pred_class == 0)

text: training_data tibble training data y Character, name response variable. Defaults "known_offender" x Vector names features used. See recipes::step_corr() information rf_trees Number trees contained ensemble. larger number trees, stable predictions - higher computational cost rf_mtry Number features sampled split rf_min_n Minimum node size (.e. number vessel-years final node ). Larger values create less complex trees, may result underfitting. Smaller values create complex trees, may result overfitting rf_reg_factor Regularization factor works penalizing new variables multiplying splitting criterion factor. result, tree biased keep splitting features already trusts, rather constantly introducing fresh ones
